extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Department of Education funds (K-12 LEAs, IHEs), school and athletic administrators, State/local education and athletic officials, athletic associations, advocates, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: A Department of Education proposed rule (NPRM) setting a regulatory standard for when and how recipients may adopt or apply sex-related criteria that would limit or deny a student's eligibility to participate on a male or female athletic team consistent with their gender identity. The document explains the proposed regulatory text, underlying legal and factual bases, and solicits public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed regulatory standard for sex-related eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts or applies sex-related criteria that would limit or deny a student's eligibility to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity, such criteria must, for each sport, level of competition, and grade or education level: (i) Be substantially related to the achievement of an important educational objective; and (ii) Minimize harms to students whose opportunity to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity would be limited or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core two-part test the Department proposes to add to 34 CFR 106.41(b). The proposed regulation does not ban sex-related criteria outright but requires recipients to satisfy this standard for any criteria that would limit or deny participation consistent with gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial relationship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex-related criteria must 'be substantially related to the achievement of an important educational objective.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department identifies prevention of sports-related injury and fairness in competition as examples of important educational objectives that courts have recognized. The analysis must be sport-, level-, and grade-specific; generalizations are insufficient. The Department notes that some uses of sex-related eligibility criteria could satisfy this requirement in particular sports, grade/education levels, and levels of competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm minimization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex-related criteria must 'minimize harms to students whose opportunity to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity would be limited or denied.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department requires recipients to consider and limit adverse effects on students excluded or limited by the criteria. The NPRM frames this as an affirmative obligation alongside the substantial relationship test; recipients should take steps that reduce negative impacts on affected students when imposing eligibility limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sport-, level-, and grade-specific application
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed requirements must be evaluated 'for each sport, level of competition, and grade or education level.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must apply the substantial relationship and harm-minimization tests separately by sport, by the level of competition (e.g., varsity, junior varsity), and by grade or education level (e.g., middle school, high school, collegiate). A single blanket policy across all sports/levels/grades is inadequate without sport- and level-specific justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal athletic opportunity across the program
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient 'must still provide equal opportunity in its athletic program as a whole' (34 CFR 106.41(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where sex-separate teams exist or are permitted under 106.41(b), recipients must ensure their overall athletic program provides equal opportunity based on sex. Disparities across the totality of the program could violate §106.41(c). The Department warns against practices (e.g., abolishing women's teams and opening only men's teams) that would not effectively accommodate interests and abilities of the excluded sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible sex-separation exception (competitive skill or contact sport)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may operate or sponsor separate teams for members of each sex where selection for such teams is based upon competitive skill or the activity involved is a contact sport (current 34 CFR 106.41(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The athletics regulation historically allowed sex-separated teams in these circumstances. The NPRM does not eliminate that exception but requires any sex-related criteria used under it to meet the proposed substantial-relationship and harm-minimization standards. Courts have recognized competitive fairness and safety as relevant in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try-out requirement when only one-sex team exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a recipient operates a team for one sex but not the other and opportunities for that excluded sex have previously been limited, members of the excluded sex 'must be allowed to try-out for the team offered unless the sport involved is a contact sport.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the longstanding athletics regulation. The NPRM reiterates this rule in discussing how sex-separation historically operated under Title IX; its submission underscores that exclusions must be narrowly applied and consistent with the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on relying on stereotypes or others' discomfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not 'adopt or adhere to requirements that rely on overly broad generalizations or stereotypes . . . or others' discomfort with transgender students.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the NPRM notes that age-appropriate, tailored requirements based on sound, current, and research-based medical knowledge about the impact of participation on competitive fairness or physical safety may be permissible, requirements cannot be based on mere stereotypes or discomfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to comply with Title IX nondiscrimination mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients that adopt or apply sex-related eligibility criteria must do so 'consistent with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate' and ensure policies do not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule seeks to clarify how recipients can ensure students have equal opportunity to participate on male and female teams as required by Title IX; recipients remain responsible for overall compliance, including providing equal opportunities and addressing disparities across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and consideration of evidence (basis for criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption or application of sex-related criteria should be informed by 'sound, current, and research-based medical knowledge' and supported by evidence demonstrating the substantial relationship to an important educational objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department based the NPRM on statutory text and legislative history, case law, State laws, policies of schools/athletic associations, and stakeholder input. Recipients should likewise rely on appropriate, sport- and level-specific evidence when justifying criteria and be prepared to document rationale consistent with the proposed standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the proposed rule (what criteria are covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM explains it would address 'sex-related criteria that would limit or deny a student's eligibility to participate on a male or female athletic team consistent with their gender identity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies the proposal is limited to sex-related eligibility criteria for male and female athletic teams; the NPRM includes examples of various approaches by athletic associations and states (included for illustration, not endorsement) and notes the proposed standard would be applied sport-, level-, and grade-specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to comment and how to file effective comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted via the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov, include the Docket ID (ED-2022-OCR-0143), and be received by the closing date (May 15, 2023). The Department generally makes comments publicly available and may redact identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maximize effect, commenters should identify the specific part of the proposed regulation or directed question each comment addresses, suggest alternatives, provide data on costs/benefits, and note ways to reduce burdens consistent with statutory objectives. If accommodations are needed for disability access or if commenters cannot use regulations.gov, contact the program contact person. Do not include information identifying others that you do not wish publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directed questions and comment content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM contains directed questions and asks commenters to help the Department comply with Executive Orders on regulatory planning (e.g., Exec. Orders 12866 and 13563) by providing information on costs, benefits, and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department requests commenters provide data or analysis to inform the Regulatory Impact Analysis—estimates of costs, benefits, baseline conditions, and alternatives. Commenters should state clearly which regulatory text or question they are addressing and may propose alternatives that reduce costs while preserving program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and non-endorsement of example policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of State and association policies included in the preamble are 'examples of various approaches' and are not required, endorsed, or indicative of compliance with the proposed standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department includes external policy excerpts for illustration only and disclaims control over their accuracy; recipients are not required to adopt examples and should not treat inclusion as legal advice or an indication of compliance.
